findings.reason: the ordered serialization §7 uses internally for exactly this reason is missing between §8 and §9, so the plan needs an s9-on-s8 edge (or the reverse) and §9 added to the followup's order list.
findings.text: §8 and §9 both declare `depends-on` s7 and nothing else, and both write `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` (§8 at plan:304; §9's first and fourth nodes at plan:322 and plan:328), while the driving followup's ordering sentence (plan:367: "§4, §6, §7 and §8 then run in order") does not mention §9 at all — so a roadmap that releases §8 when s7 lands also releases §9's first node, and two workers edit one file

findings.reason: the headline figure is a claim the plan makes about its own outcome and now contradicts its own sections; the earlier review declined exactly this line on the arithmetic §9 has since invalidated.
findings.text: §1 says the fold "leaves 65 visible leaves, or 66 if §4 finds `crew merge` still landing heads", but the arithmetic that produced 65/66 counted §6 as removing all five read verbs (-4); §6 has since landed keeping all five (plan:175-177) and §9 now retires only `list`, `ledger` and `velocity` (-2 with §6's added `crew view`), so the same accounting yields 67, or 68 with `crew merge` retained — and §4's evidence says `crew merge` is retained (plan:212-213), making the current sentence wrong by two

findings.reason: as written the node cannot produce its own required evidence and stops as blocked on a write-scope refusal, so either the capture moves to the node that owns the test file or that file joins the mover's fence.
findings.text: the done-when requires "Each retired verb's answers are captured as fixtures at the base of the node that moves its callers", covering `crew list` with `--project`, `--phase`, `--mine` and `--session`, but the node that moves `crew list`'s callers (`cso-list-callers-move-to-crew-view`) does not list `tests/test_read_verbs_retire_behind_crew_view.py` among its write paths (plan:326), the file those fixtures must be recorded in

findings.reason: the keep-`directory`-visible count rests on a caller census, and this citation is a false positive in it; the decision still stands on the verified imas-ambix caller (ops/lane-cycle/AGENTS.md:40), but the census claim itself needs correcting before it is quoted as evidence.
findings.text: §9's Why asserts "`crew directory` is invoked by `skills/reckon-build/scripts/worktree_fleet.py` and by a guide in another project", but that script contains no invocation of the verb: every occurrence of "directory" in it is a local variable for the config directory, and it reads live run pointers directly rather than shelling out ("Read live run pointers directly from the transient crew directory", worktree_fleet.py:126)
